title: Pocket bench catalog — microburst recipes & quick heuristics
content:
Notes to self / pocket bench cookbook (raw)

Context:
- Trying lightweight, reproducible microburst recipes that I can run on a single A100-40GB instance in the dev fleet.
- Goal: small, interpretable tweaks that lower p99 tail without regressing median throughput. Keep configs small so SRE can run quickly.
- Hypothesis: modest active batching + short KV cache TTL + small prefill priming reduces p99 by absorbing token spikes but avoids big throughput regression.

Environment:
- model: llama-13b-8bit-quant (dev-quant-2024a)
- infra: dev-a100-1 (A100 40GB), gRPC frontend -> inference pool (single worker)
- runtime flags: --batcher=adaptive --batch-window-ms=8/16/32 (sweep) --kv-ttl=0/1s/3s --prefill=off/on(2q)
- client: bench-client v0.9 (poisson arrival util)

Quick run plan (local):
1) baseline: no prefill, batch-window=8ms, kv-ttl=0s, arrival poisson mean=50req/s (1–2s context). 3x5m runs.
2) microburst: inject 3s pulses: 300req/s for 2s every 30s.
3) sweep batch-window {8,16,32}, kv-ttl {0,1,3}, prefill {off,on} -> measure p50,p95,p99, qps achieved, error rate.

Raw results (summarized, median of 3 runs):

Run | batch-win | kv-ttl | prefill | avg-qps | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | err% | notes
----+-----------+--------+---------+--------+---------+---------+---------+------+-
B1   | 8ms       | 0s     | off     | 48.2   | 32      | 110     | 320     | 0.4  | baseline small jitter
M1   | 8ms       | 1s     | on(2q)  | 45.6   | 36      | 95      | 220     | 0.6  | lower tail, slight qps drop
M2   | 16ms      | 1s     | on(2q)  | 44.0   | 40      | 88      | 180     | 0.7  | sweet spot for p99 vs qps
M3   | 32ms      | 3s     | on(2q)  | 38.5   | 50      | 105     | 160     | 1.2  | p99 improved but p50 regressed a lot
M4   | 8ms       | 3s     | off     | 46.8   | 34      | 130     | 340     | 0.8  | long kv-ttl w/o prefill hurts p95

Observations and interpretations:
- Prefill with short window (2 queued tokens) + modest batch-window (16ms) gave the best tradeoff: p99 ~180ms vs baseline 320ms while qps only ~9% lower.
- Large batch-windows (32ms) reduce p99 further only at cost of substantial median latency and throughput (see M3). Not acceptable for API tier.
- Long kv-ttl (3s) without prefill increases p95/p99 in some cases -> suggests stale KV caching causing head-of-line penalties when requests have divergent contexts.
- Error rate correlated with higher batch sizes under spike (OOM-ish backpressure spikes), need to monitor allocator fragmentation.

Mini-checklist for next run (dev -> sim cluster):
- add allocator metrics: fragmentation %, gpu-mem-snapshots at 1s intervals
- instrument batch composition (how many distinct contexts per batch)
- try prefill size {1,2,4} to find minimal effective prefill
- test with short sequence lengths vs long (avg token per request 40 vs 200)

Quick heuristics (ops playbook blurb):
- If p99 > target and p50 within budget: try batch-window=16ms + prefill=2 + kv-ttl=1s.
- If p50 regresses > 20%: back off batch-window to 8ms or disable prefill.
- Avoid kv-ttl>2s on heterogeneous-context workloads.

Notes to hand to SRE/runbook (very rough):
- Config snippet to apply in canary: 
  batcher: adaptive
  batch-window-ms: 16
  prefill-queued-tokens: 2
  kv-cache-ttl-seconds: 1
- Watch windows: p50/p95/p99 in 1m/5m; gpu-mem fragmentation; batch composition entropy

Oddities and loose hypotheses:
- I saw occasional microspikes where p99 jumped because a single large request (~1.1k tokens) mixed in with many 40-token requests; suspect our packing policy lets a big request anchor a batch. Need to record max token in batch and try pack-by-size or cap-per-batch.
- Poisson pulses sometimes under-estimate real client bursts (client-side retries create correlated arrivals). We should try a heavy-tailed arrival (Weibull/Log-normal) next.

Scratch lists / TODOs:
- [ ] run larger sweep on sim-cluster (3 nodes) with same configs
- [ ] add logging for batch token distribution + sample payloads (no PII)
- [ ] open PR to add prefill flag to canary config templates (link to PR above)
- [ ] validate with long sequences (200-800 tokens)

Clipping of raw traces (for quick glance):
- timeline excerpt (p99 vs qps during a pulse):

  time   | qps | p99_ms
  00:00  | 50  | 310
  00:12  | 49  | 325
  00:30  | 300 | 520  <-- pulse starts
  00:32  | 300 | 780  <-- baseline
  00:33  | 300 | 220  <-- prefill+16ms run shows drop within 3s
  00:36  | 50  | 140  <-- post-pulse recovery

Random notes to self: short writeups like this should live in "users/" so new hires can run them quickly. Keep recipes stamped with hardware + flags + small ascii results.

— Zenobia
